--- title: "AE06-03 Simpson's paradox and unobserved heterogeneity" date: "2026-09-23" output: html_document: code_folding: show editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- # Setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(alr4) library(GGally) library(parameters) library(performance) library(see) library(car) library(broom) library(modelsummary) library(texreg) library(correlation) library(patchwork) library(lmtest) library(sandwich) library(clubSandwich) library(forcats) library(modelbased) library(emmeans) library(ggeffects) knitr::opts_chunk$set( fig.align = "center", fig.width = 16, fig.asp = 0.618, fig.retina = 1, out.width = "100%", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, echo = TRUE ) ``` ::: # Goals: Learn about vicious role of Heteroskedasticity # The problem: Let us understand how bill depth affects the bill length in penguins Check: [https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/lter_penguins.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/culmen_depth.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: # Data ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) pings <- penguins ``` ::: # Summary stats ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} pings %>% datasummary_skim() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ggpairs(pings) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ae06-03-simpsons-paradox_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: # Fit and summary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} ping_fit1 <- lm(bill_length_mm ~ bill_depth_mm + sex, pings) parameters(ping_fit1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Parameter | Coefficient | SE | 95% CI | t(330) | p --------------------------------------------------------------------- (Intercept) | 61.00 | 2.35 | [56.38, 65.62] | 26.00 | < .001 bill depth mm | -1.15 | 0.14 | [-1.43, -0.87] | -8.16 | < .001 sex [male] | 5.44 | 0.55 | [ 4.35, 6.54] | 9.81 | < .001 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} performance(ping_fit1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # Indices of model performance AIC | AICc | BIC | R2 | R2 (adj.) | RMSE | Sigma ------------------------------------------------------------ 1980.5 | 1980.6 | 1995.7 | 0.266 | 0.262 | 4.677 | 4.699 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} check_model(ping_fit1, check = c("linearity", "homogeneity")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](ae06-03-simpsons-paradox_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){fig-align='center' width=100%} ::: ::: # Check assumpation ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(lmtest) bptest(ping_fit1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` studentized Breusch-Pagan test data: ping_fit1 BP = 36.958, df = 2, p-value = 9.431e-09 ``` ::: ::: # Correct SE ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} parameters(ping_fit1, vcov = "HC5") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Parameter | Coefficient | SE | 95% CI | t(330) | p --------------------------------------------------------------------- (Intercept) | 61.00 | 1.92 | [57.23, 64.77] | 31.80 | < .001 bill depth mm | -1.15 | 0.12 | [-1.39, -0.91] | -9.46 | < .001 sex [male] | 5.44 | 0.53 | [ 4.41, 6.48] | 10.33 | < .001 ``` ::: ::: # Exploring relationship between bill_length_mm and bill_depth_mm ## Step 1.
